llm.summary: This skill performs pet-grooming media analysis, but it also silently creates or uses a remote-linked identity and stores tokens locally, so users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: Uploading local media or forwarding URLs to the analysis API is purpose-aligned, but the runtime also reads OpenClaw identity environment variables, OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE, and data/smyx-api-key.txt and creates workspace data/skills directories.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time shell hook, obfuscation, or destructive setup was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, but the included shared common code carries network, database, and credential helpers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs automatic cloud history queries and internal identity handling while suppressing identity/API-key parameters from normal user help, reducing clear user control over account-linked actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates a shared SQLite database in the workspace data directory and can store username, realname, email, token, and open_token values after automatic remote login/registration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core media-analysis and history-report functions fit the stated purpose, but the implementation also performs automatic identity creation/login and token handling that is broader than grooming analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pet images/videos or supplied media URLs being sent to lifeemergence.com/open.lifeemergence.com services and with the skill automatically creating or reusing an internal account identity, storing API tokens in a local workspace database, and using that identity to retrieve cloud history reports.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local file access, command execution, and network API calls are expected for this script-driven analysis skill, but the artifact does not give tight permission or consent boundaries for uploads, identity use, or endpoint scope.
[SQP-2] expected: Forwarding a media file or URL to the lifeemergence analysis API is central to the skill and generally disclosed; the remaining concern is that identity binding, token use, and data-handling details are not clearly surfaced to users.
[SDI-1] expected: History report listing is documented in SKILL.md and implemented through the cloud page API, so it is not hidden; it still depends on implicit identity resolution and can return user-linked report URLs.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The common utilities read or create an internal open-id, read a workspace smyx-api-key file, call a silent remote phoneLogin/register flow, and persist auth fields locally, which is not adequately scoped for simple grooming analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The shared API service exposes generic HTTP/CRUD helpers, and RequestUtil attaches auth headers to supplied absolute URLs; reviewed first-party skill paths mostly use relative endpoints, so this supports Review rather than malicious classification.
[E1] unexpected: The external registration/login POST is artifact-backed and distinct from media analysis upload; it sends generated identity values to the remote health service without a separate user-directed onboarding step.
[SQP-1] expected: Triggering on grooming media and explicit history-report phrases is consistent with the stated purpose; I did not treat this alone as a Review basis, though upload intent should be clear.
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic getattr filters are present in the generic DAO, but they are not shown as exposed to arbitrary user filters in the main CLI path and are not code execution by themselves, so I downgraded this concern.
